knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum and Constant Factor Rules

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x^{5}+7}{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(x^{3} + \frac{7}{x^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\int x^{3}\,\mathrm{d}x+7\int x^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\left(\frac{x^{4}}{4}\right)+7\left(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{7}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x^{8}-6}{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(2 x^{6} - \frac{6}{x^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\int x^{6}\,\mathrm{d}x-6\int x^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\left(\frac{x^{7}}{7}\right)-6\left(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{2x^{7}}{7}+\frac{6}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

The blank excludes the constant $C$, which is already supplied.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \sqrt{x}\left(x+3\right)\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(x^{\frac{3}{2}} + 3 \sqrt{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\int x^{\frac{3}{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x+3\int x^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\left(\frac{x^{\frac{5}{2}}}{\frac{5}{2}}\right)+3\left(\frac{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{2\sqrt{x^{5}}}{5}+2\sqrt{x^{3}}+C.\end{aligned}
